correctness.rationale: A fixed representative is exactly a point of (I-R)^(-1)Z^2 in the half-open square. For u=cot(theta/2)>0 the integer labels obey 0<=a<3 and -1<b<2, with a=0 forcing the origin. Of (1,0),(1,1),(2,0),(2,1), (2,0) lands on the excluded right edge, and the others pass the half-open inequalities exactly at u<2,1,1/2 respectively (none at equality). Coordinate exchange conjugates the opposite rotation; the half-turn has exactly the four half-lattice representatives. At an interior fixed point the rotation followed by its integer correction rotates the entire boundary-distance open disk onto itself, and this radius is maximal among centered disks contained in Q. The displayed coordinate distances give the radii. Disjointness also follows directly: a shared point of two such disks would have the same unique floor correction for two distinct centers, impossible since I-R is injective. The area sum and normalized area invariance follow; each new radius vanishes linearly at its own threshold, with nonzero slope because |du/dtheta|=(1+u^2)/2.
